title: ci: upgrade Actions for Node 24; replace Ana06/get-changed-files
description:
Upgrade GitHub Actions used in this repo to versions that run on **Node 24**, and replace the unmaintained `Ana06/get-changed-files@v2.3.0` action (Node 20) with a small local Python helper.

This addresses [GitHub’s Node 20 deprecation on Actions runners](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-09-19-deprecation-of-node-20-on-github-actions-runners/).

### Action bumps

| Action | From | To | Runtime |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `actions/checkout` | v4 | v6 | node24 |
| `actions/setup-java` | v3 | v5 | node24 |
| `docker/login-action` | v1 | v4 | node24 |
| `docker/build-push-action` | v2 / v3 | v7 | node24 |
| `actions/github-script` | v6 | v8 | node24 |
| `Ana06/get-changed-files` | v2.3.0 | local Python | n/a |

### Other workflow changes

- **Build results:** replace `styfle/cancel-workflow-action@0.9.1` with native `concurrency` (`cancel-in-progress: true`).
- **Changed files:** `inst/gha/get-changed-files.py` lists PR files via the GitHub API (paginated) and writes `all` as a JSON array to `GITHUB_OUTPUT`, matching prior `format: json` / `outputs.all` usage.
- Call sites use `python3` and `GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}`.
- Unit tests in `inst/gha/test_get_changed_files.py` (pagination, empty result, HTTP errors, GITHUB_OUTPUT).

### Why not keep Ana06?

`Ana06/get-changed-files@v2.3.0` is the latest release and still targets Node 20, with no Node 24 release. A stdlib-only script avoids third-party Node actions for this one use case.

title: fix: resolve race conditions in snapshot-info-option
description:
**Problem:** The JavaScript client previously used a polling loop (wait()) to query the snapshot endpoint, which often occurred before the R server finished setting and flushing reactive input/output updates. This resulted in false-positive validation failures on slower environments.

**Solution:** Refactored the synchronization logic using custom message handlers (snapshot-ready) and session$onFlushed(). The client now waits for an explicit server acknowledgment that the inputs have been received and processed before initiating the HTTP snapshot request. (This matches the pattern recently implemented to fix 226-snapshot-info-url).

title: Validate current snapshot platform for app 313
description:
## Summary

- validate that app 313 has snapshots for the current platform variant
- allow snapshots for older platform variants to remain alongside the current variant
- accept four fresh macOS 4.6 snapshots generated by CI

## Root cause

The validation used `identical(dir("_snaps"), platform_variant())`. That comparison can only succeed when `_snaps` contains exactly one directory. With both `mac-4.5` and `mac-4.6` present, the macOS release job incorrectly reported `Outdated snaps folder found!` even though the required `mac-4.6` directory existed.

This applies the same membership check already used by apps 193, 301, and 302. Once the test ran, CI produced updated macOS 4.6 images; these were accepted with `fix_snaps()` from `gha-d622496-2026_07_12_05_06-4.6-macOS`.

## Validation

- reproduced the two-folder validation failure
- verified the membership condition accepts the current platform when multiple variants exist
- parsed the complete R test file successfully
- ran `fix_snaps()` against the PR SHA
- verified all four accepted PNGs are byte-for-byte identical to their CI `.new.png` files
- verified no `.new` files, `sysinfo` churn, or generated artifacts remain
- ran `git diff --check`

The pushed snapshots trigger a fresh macOS release CI run for end-to-end validation.

title: Fix failing nightly test apps on main
description:
Fixes the app test failures from the nightly run https://github.com/rstudio/shinycoreci/actions/runs/29175987061

## What was failing and why

| App | Jobs | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| 110-error-sanitization | ubuntu-oldrel-1/4, macos-release | Screenshot `006.png` drifted past the fuzzy threshold (conv ~44 > 5) on linux-4.2, linux-4.5, mac-4.6 |
| 301-bs-themes, 302-bootswatch-themes, 304-bslib-card | macos-release | Committed mac-4.6 snapshots don't match what the macOS release runner actually renders (conv up to ~11.8k > 3000) |
| 313-bslib-card-tab-focus | macos-release | `Outdated snaps folder found!` — `_snaps/` contained both `mac-4.5` and `mac-4.6` |
| 226-snapshot-info-url (and 225 in the previous run) | macos-oldrel-4 | The UTF-8 items (`åå`, `∫∫`) no longer round-trip/sort as C-locale order on the mac R 4.2 arm64 runner |

## Fixes

- **110 / 301 / 302 / 304**: accepted the CI-generated snapshots (`*.new.png` / `*.new.json`) that the failing run pushed to its `gha-6c4f15d-*` branches, so the committed snapshots now match what CI renders.
- **301 / 302 / 313**: removed stale `mac-4.5` snapshot folders (these apps only screenshot on mac + r-release, now 4.6).
- **313**: also removed the `mac-4.6` PNGs — they were byte-identical copies of the old mac-4.5 (R 4.5-era) images and were never validated on the current runner. With no `_snaps` folder the outdated-folder check passes and the next nightly run will generate fresh, CI-authentic snapshots on its `gha-` branch, which can then be committed.
- **225 / 226**: use the ASCII-only item set (same as Windows) on macOS with R < 4.3, and include the *received* names in the FAIL status message so the next diagnosis doesn't require guesswork (the old message only printed the expected names).

title: Fix GHA test results push retry loop and update nightly snapshots
description:
### Summary

This PR resolves issues in the GHA nightly runs and updates the app snapshots and system info text files to match the latest nightly run baseline.

### Changes

#### 1. GitHub Workflows
* **Robust Branch Cleanup**: Added `trap 'git checkout ${{ steps.current_branch.outputs.name }}' EXIT` to both the push steps in `.github/workflows/apps-test-os.yml`. This guarantees that even if pushing fails, the workspace is always checked back out to the original branch (avoiding subsequent checkout failures in post-run cleanup steps due to missing action files on the `_test_results` branch).
* **Retry Loop Fix**: Corrected the post-increment arithmetic `((counter++))` to `counter=$((counter + 1))`. Since `counter` starts at `0`, the post-increment evaluated to `0` (exit code `1`), which instantly aborted the script under `-e`.
* **Sleep Syntax Update**: Modernized the deprecated arithmetic syntax `$[ ($RANDOM % 10) + 5 ]s` to standard `$(( (RANDOM % 10) + 5 ))`.

#### 2. App Snapshots & System Info
* Accepted all updated nightly snapshots and package variants (`inst/apps/.../_snaps/` and `inst/apps/sysinfo-*.txt` files) from the 15 nightly run branches matching commit `ec580f43a32ca881a623630d83572c216bc6d2f4`.

title: Stabilize CI snapshot fonts and chart rendering
description:
## Summary

This PR makes Shiny app snapshot tests less sensitive to GitHub runner, OS font, and graphics-device drift.

It vendors a small Noto font set, registers it during app tests, injects the same font setup into browser screenshots, and ensures Shiny child processes started by `shinytest2::AppDriver` use the same rendering defaults. It also pins CI runner labels instead of using mutable `*-latest` labels.

## Why

Recent CI failures were caused by snapshot churn from OS/browser font changes and chart label rendering differences, not real app behavior changes.

## Notes

This may cause one expected snapshot baseline update after merge. After that, future snapshot diffs should be less frequent and more meaningful.

title: Port pkgcheck-* action scripts from bash to Python
description:
## Summary

Convert the eight bash scripts that back the `pkgcheck-*` composite actions (added in #350) to Python 3, replacing the `gh` + `jq` + `git` pipelines with stdlib-based equivalents that still shell out to `gh` and `git` for auth and plumbing. Caller-visible behavior is unchanged: each composite action's `env:` contract is the same, and step outputs / step-summary lines / `::error::` annotations / exit codes match the bash version.

Two commits:

- **Port pkgcheck-* composite action scripts from bash to Python** — replaces all eight `.sh` files with `.py` equivalents and points each `action.yaml` step at `python3 "$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/foo.py"`. The verifier-prepare step in `pkgcheck-create-pr` stages `verify.py` into `RUNNER_TEMP` (no `chmod` needed since invocation is via `python3`, not a shebang).
- **Use block-scalar form for run: invocations in pkgcheck actions** — switches the seven script-invocation steps from `run: python3 "..."` to the `run: |` multi-line form so they match the style already used by the verifier-prepare step and the inline shell snippets in the same files.

### What got cleaner

- `gh api ... | jq -s ...` for paginated issue lookup → a small concatenated-JSON decoder + a list comprehension.
- `printf '%s\n' ... | here-string` body assembly → `"\n".join(lines)`.
- `set +e` / `set -e` wrappers → ordinary `try` / `check=False` returncodes.
- Workflow-name slug sanitization is two `re.sub` calls instead of `tr | sed -E 's/-+/-/g; s/^-//; s/-\$//'`.
- The dispatched-run picking heuristic (created-after-dispatch + bot-actor preference, oldest-first fallback) is now a plain function shared in spirit between `verify.py` and `watch-remote-run.py`.

### What's preserved

- Same `\$GITHUB_OUTPUT` keys (`issue_url`, `issue_number`, `issue_mode`, `existing_pr_url`, `pr_url`, `pr_number`, `branch`, `pushed`, `conclusion`, `run_url`, `run_id`, `attempt`, `should_open_issue`, `run_conclusion`).
- Same console messages and `::error::` / `::warning::` / `::notice::` annotations.
- Same git plumbing in `finalize-pr` / `finalize-retry-commit`: same commit messages, same branch-name slug rules, same `x-access-token` remote, same fall-through merge sources for the squash-retry path.
- Same conclusion → `should_open_issue` mapping in `watch-remote-run.py` (only \`failure / timed_out / action_required / startup_failure / stale\` open issues).
- Same remediation marker, same label color/description, same title fallback, same body markdown for `create-or-reuse-issue.py`.

## Test plan

- [ ] \`python3 -m py_compile\` passes for all 8 scripts (already verified locally).
- [ ] Trigger \`external-package-checks\` via \`workflow_dispatch\` against a known-passing target and confirm: dispatch step succeeds, watch step reports \`success\`, no remediation issue is opened, job passes.
- [ ] Trigger \`external-package-checks\` against a known-failing target without \`bedrock-role-to-assume\` and confirm: a remediation issue is created (or reused if one already exists), \`existing_pr_url\` is empty when none exists, job fails with the expected step-summary block.
- [ ] Trigger \`external-package-checks\` against a known-failing target with Bedrock configured and confirm: remediation PR is opened, verify-1 dispatches and watches the PR-branch run, retry path runs (or doesn't) per \`max-attempts\`, final-status comment is posted to both the issue and the PR, throwaway retry branch is deleted on success.
- [ ] Specifically exercise the squash-retry path in \`finalize-retry-commit.py\` (Claude opens its own retry branch) at least once.
- [ ] Confirm \`gh pr list --jq '.[0].url // empty'\` still returns an empty string when no PR exists for the branch (kept the same flag rather than parsing JSON in Python).

title: Add Shiny team agentic issue triage workflow (Bedrock, dry-run, scoped to rstudio/reactlog)
description:
## Summary

Adds a scheduled and manually-dispatched cross-repo issue triage workflow that runs Anthropic Claude via **AWS Bedrock** (no direct Anthropic API or Copilot endpoints) against an explicit allowlist of repositories.

The initial allowlist is **just `rstudio/reactlog`** because that is the only non-shinycoreci repo the `posit-shiny-automation` GitHub App is currently installed on. Onboarding more repos later is a one-line edit to [.github/triage/team-issue-triage.yaml](.github/triage/team-issue-triage.yaml) once the App is installed there.

## What this adds

- `.github/workflows/team-issue-triage.yml` — the workflow. Reads its repo allowlist + report destination from YAML at runtime; assumes an AWS IAM role via OIDC; runs `anthropics/claude-code-action@v1.0.92` with `use_bedrock: true`; validates Claude's structured output before any GitHub write.
- `.github/triage/team-issue-triage.yaml` — single source of truth: `repositories:`, `report_repo:`, scan settings, engine constraints, project mapping.
- `.github/triage/labels.yaml` — fixed allowlist of labels the AI may apply.
- `.github/triage/issue-triage-rubric.md` — decision rubric.
- `.github/triage/state-template/cursors.json` — bootstrap state for new repos.
- `.github/triage/README.md` — operator setup + 'Adding More Repositories' guide.
- `.github/agentic-issue-triage.md` — design doc.
- Triage state is durably committed to the long-lived `triage-state` branch (not main).

## Required org/repo configuration

Already present at the **org** level on rstudio: `POSIT_SHINY_AUTOMATION_CLIENT_ID`, `POSIT_SHINY_AUTOMATION_PEM`. Already present at the **repo** level on rstudio/shinycoreci: `AWS_BEDROCK_ROLE_TO_ASSUME` (OIDC role with `bedrock:InvokeModel` for the Anthropic family). `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` is hardcoded to `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` in the workflow env for now.

## Safety posture

- **Dry-run by default.** `TRIAGE_APPLY_WRITES` defaults to `false`; `workflow_dispatch` input `apply_writes` also defaults to `false`. No labels, comments, or project items are written until explicitly toggled.
- The Claude step receives a **read-only** GitHub App token. The post-processing JS step uses a **separate** issue-write token.
- The validator hard-codes (a) the YAML-derived repo allowlist, (b) the YAML label allowlist, (c) max items, (d) max comment / report sizes. Anything Claude returns outside those bounds aborts the run.
- Workflow forbids `api.anthropic.com`, `statsig.anthropic.com`, `api.githubcopilot.com`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, and `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`.

## Test plan

After merge, dispatch from `triage-state` against a synthetic test issue on `rstudio/reactlog` with `apply_writes=false` and inspect the step summary.

```bash
gh workflow run team-issue-triage.yml --repo rstudio/shinycoreci --ref triage-state \
  -f apply_writes=false -f scan_since=2026-05-04T00:00:00Z
```

If preview output looks reasonable, create the workflow's label taxonomy on each onboarded repo (loop in [.github/triage/README.md](.github/triage/README.md)), then enable writes.

title: Update GitHub Actions versions and PR file logic
description:
Bump workflow actions: replace actions/checkout@v4 with @v6 across multiple workflows, upgrade actions/setup-java@v3 to @v5, and actions/github-script@v6 to @v8. Replace Ana06/get-changed-files steps with a gh api paginated call that collects PR file names (writes JSON to GITHUB_OUTPUT) and adds GH_TOKEN/env + bash execution. These changes modernize CI actions and improve reliability of PR file collection.

The issue is that actions/checkout@v6 no longer sets the http.https://github.com/.extraheader git config. The git config --unset for a non-existent key returns exit code 5, and because the commands were chained with &&, it failed the entire step.

Fixed all 3 affected files by adding || true so the unset gracefully handles missing keys:
The error is git config --local --unset http.https://github.com/.extraheader — exit code 5 means the key doesn't exist. With actions/checkout@v6, this header is no longer set, so the unset command fails and (because of && chaining) takes down the whole step.

title: Add 312-bslib-sidebar-resize
description:
Adds a manual testing app for plot and output resizing in sidebars (without cards).

Pairs with https://github.com/rstudio/bslib/pull/566 where this behavior is improved for sidebars.

## Expected behavior

In the app below, both the "static" ggplot2 output and the htmlwidget plotly plot output will stretch during the sidebar transition. The static plot will re-render when the transition is complete, so there's a small "snap" when the new plot is rendered. (No snap is seen in the case of an htmlwidget like plotly.)

All plots stretch during resize when the shared sidebar is toggled; only the sidebar in the local sidebar layout stretches when the local sidebar is toggled.


https://github.com/rstudio/shinycoreci/assets/5420529/2786af49-ca02-4ae6-8fe2-ad121c5946e7



## Failing behavior

When the behavior isn't present, neither the plot nor the htmlwidget's will update its width until after receiving a re-render event from the server.



https://github.com/rstudio/shinycoreci/assets/5420529/fe0c8153-2ac2-4022-91f7-92ff499696ad

The sidebar dependencies are not present on page load but are included when the sidebars are added via `insertUI()`. We test general function and form of the sidebar, in particular around initialization state and the collapse toggle event handlers that would not work correctly if the sidebar dependencies did not include special post-page-load initialization methods.

2. `311-bslib-sidebar-toggle-methods` tests the tab focus order of nested sidebars and all of the related sidebar toggling methods, including server-side `sidebar_toggle()`.

description:
This adds a new `testthat.yml` workflow for running `testthat`/unit/integration tests on any application containing a `tests/testthat.R` file. `testthat.R` is sourced via `shiny::runTests()`, so code in apps with an `R/` directory (like module code) is loaded before any test-related code is executed.

This PR also adds a new `shinycoreci::trigger()` function that can be used to programmatically trigger workflows from the R console.

The testthat workflow won't be exercised until https://github.com/rstudio/shinycoreci-apps/pull/2 adds apps to test, but adding it beforehand should be fine (it will do nothing).
